summary: # Marvelous Designer Tips and Tricks Class ## Introduction Hello, everyone! This is Yamagio's little class. Today, I will give you a few tips on using Marvelous Designer (MD) that will make your clothing-making process more efficient, allowing you to finish faster. ## Finding Lost Pattern Pieces First of all, when we are making clothes, it is possible for the garments to accidentally move out of our visible area. What should we do in this situation? Do we have to keep moving around to find it? In fact, you don't need to keep searching. Instead, simply right-click on a blank area and select "Zoom to the Whole Scene." This will bring your garment back into view. ### Locating in 2D Similarly, when working in the 2D interface, if you want to find a pattern piece that has moved out of sight, you can still use the same method. Right-click and click on "Zoom to the Whole Scene," and your version will reappear. ## Precise Movement of Pattern Pieces The second little trick involves moving pattern pieces precisely. For instance, if you want to change the shape of a pattern, how do you enter an exact value? First, move the piece to the desired location. Then, click on the right arrow key on your keyboard to enter the precise distance you want to move it. For example, you might want to move it 8 centimeters. Just fine! You can do this for the other side as well. Move it to the left, press the right arrow key, and enter 8 centimeters. This way, you can accurately adjust your values. ## Copying and Pasting Values Now, let's move on to our third MD trick: copying and pasting values. When making items like belts, you often need to add holes or internal patterns. Do you have to keep drawing each hole and then press Ctrl+C and Ctrl+V to paste it repeatedly? Thankfully, it doesn't have to be that complicated. Simply draw one internal pattern, then move it for better visibility. After that, use Ctrl+C to copy it, and Ctrl+V to paste. If you need to move the pasted version, right-click and click on "Scale." Adjust the scale based on the distance you want and choose the color you prefer. Once you’re satisfied, you can convert the internal pattern to a hole, and voilà! The hole is created. ## Conclusion That wraps up this episode of Yamagio's little class. In the next episode, I will continue to share more Marvelous Designer tips and tricks. Stay tuned!
